des_teaser.label: Teaser — stadium floodlight hero

content.prompt: Cinematic moody stadium photograph: single floodlight cutting through dust and rain, illuminating one celebrating silhouette on an empty field, rich teal-amber palette, 35mm film grain, no text

des_teaser.brief: Full-bleed hero image at the very top of the page — a single silhouetted figure under a lone stadium spotlight, rest of the arena dark. Sets the tone: one lit moment, everything else in shadow. Layered under the title and subtitle with a dark gradient overlay so text stays legible.
des_teaser.rationale: A video teaser would be heavier and less mood-forward. A single moody still matches the blog's editorial tone and mirrors the story shape (one lit moment in a dark field).

des_01.label: Dontrelle Willis spike chart (hook)

highlight.annotation: 22 wins, 2.63 ERA, NL Cy Young runner-up

style.palette: single amber highlight on peak, muted grey line elsewhere
style.y_axis: log-scale so rank 8 and rank 1338 can coexist

des_01.brief: A line chart of Dontrelle Willis's MLB career rank from 2003 to 2011. Y-axis is rank (inverted, so up means better, with log scale so rank 8 and rank 1338 are both visible). One sharp peak at 2005 highlighted in warm amber, all other points and the connecting line in muted grey. A subtle annotation labels the peak ('22 wins, 2.63 ERA'). A second annotation at rank 1338 labels '3 years later.' This is the headline visual.
des_01.rationale: The spike shape IS the story. A single clean line with one highlighted point makes the arc instantly readable.

des_02.label: Dana Barros spike chart (hook supporting)

style.palette: single cool-blue highlight on peak, muted grey line

des_02.brief: Same chart grammar as des_01, a half-size secondary chart stacked immediately below or beside it. Dana Barros NBA career 1990-2004, peak 1995 at rank 8 highlighted in cool blue. Places the two hook arcs side by side so the reader sees the same shape in two sports.
des_02.rationale: Pairing two spikes from two sports makes the pattern feel universal rather than cherry-picked.

des_03.label: Headline stat — 78 of 1,076

content.label: of 1,076 elite careers across 8 leagues had exactly one top-20 season and never came close again — 7.2%.

des_03.brief: A single enormous stat: '78' in a very large serif numeral (about 120px on desktop), followed by the smaller 'of 1,076 elite careers...' subtitle line. Sits below the definition paragraphs in edt_02. Muted amber numeral on dark background.
des_03.rationale: The headline number of the whole piece deserves to be big.

des_04.label: League breakdown — horizontal bar

style.palette: sequential warm (lightest for lowest pct) with MLB and WNBA labels emphasized

des_04.brief: Horizontal bar chart, 8 bars (one per league), sorted from MLB (15.5%) at the top to WNBA (0.8%) at the bottom. MLB bar in saturated orange, WNBA in muted grey, others in a gradient between. Each bar labeled with its percentage AND 'n=32 of 206' style count. The contrast between MLB top and WNBA bottom is the point.
des_04.rationale: A horizontal bar is the clearest presentation of a single-dimension comparison across 8 categories. Sorting emphasizes the ordering.

des_05.label: Peak rank distribution — histogram

style.palette: warm gradient — bars at rank 1-5 in cool, rank 16-20 in warm

des_05.brief: A histogram of exact peak rank values (1 through 20), bar for each rank, height = number of one-hit wonders with that peak. Reveals the skew toward 17-19. Annotation arrow pointing to rank 17 with label 'most common peak'.
des_05.rationale: Using the exact-rank histogram (17 buckets) rather than the 4-bucket summary shows the full shape of the distribution — more texture, more 'aha'.

des_06.label: Career timing — when did the peak happen?

style.palette: single hue, with the year 4-6 bar in highlight

des_06.brief: A bar chart with 5 bars (year 1, year 2-3, year 4-6, year 7-10, year 11+). Year 4-6 is tallest at 25 and should be highlighted. Caption beneath: 'Median peak: career year 5'.
des_06.rationale: Busts the 'rookie sensation' stereotype with one clean visual.

des_07.label: Peak-to-next-year drop by league

style.palette: single warm color, opacity faded for small-n leagues (n<=2)
style.axis_label_x: Median rank drop, peak year → next season

des_07.brief: A horizontal bar chart like des_04 but showing median one-year drop in rank positions. MLB (132) and NHL (118) at the top; ATP (41) at the bottom. Bars for leagues with small samples (n<=2) shown at reduced opacity with a footnote caveat.
des_07.rationale: Reinforces the league-level story with a different metric — the speed of the fall.

des_08.label: Canonical eight — interactive gallery

content.initial_state: All 8 canonical one-hit wonders shown as a row/grid of portrait cards. Each card has: player portrait (or initial if no portrait), name, league, peak year, peak rank, median rank. First card (Dana Barros) selected by default, showing their full career trajectory chart in a larger panel to the right of or below the grid.
content.trigger: Click any card to switch the trajectory chart to that player
content.transition: Smooth tween between two line charts: the old line fades down to 20% opacity and persists as a ghost so the reader can compare shapes; the new player's line animates in with its peak year highlighted.
content.payoff: The reader sees that all 8 canonical OHWs have the same characteristic shape — one tall spike on a flat background — across 8 different sports. Ghost lines make this comparison visceral.

des_08.brief: Eight portrait cards along the top: Dana Barros (NBA), Dontrelle Willis (MLB), Jiri Hudler (NHL), Rich Beem (PGA), Hilary Lunke (LPGA), Martin Verkerk (ATP), Karolina Sprem (WTA), Tracy Reid (WNBA). Use the Detective's ref_ images for the four with portraits (Barros, Willis, Hudler, Beem) and a monogram tile for the other four. Clicking a card updates a large line chart below (y = rank, inverted, log; x = career year index). Previously selected players' lines stay on the chart as thin grey 'ghost lines' so the reader sees the same spike shape repeat.
des_08.rationale: Gallery-style interactions create engagement without overwhelming. Ghost lines is the clever bit: they let the reader visually confirm 'yes, it's the same shape' across 8 sports.

des_09.label: Spike motif image — section break

content.prompt: Minimal editorial illustration: tall thin vertical spike of warm light rising out of a horizontal line of smaller bumps, midnight-navy background, glowing golden-orange spike tip, abstract statistical line, no text

des_09.brief: Use as a thin horizontal banner between the canonical-eight gallery and the extreme-tail section — the geometric version of the shape the charts are showing.
des_09.rationale: A visual motif helps the reader internalize the shape of the story.

des_10.label: Most extreme OHWs — ranked table

content.interaction: hover tooltip with peak_rank, median_rank, peak_year

style.palette: categorical — each league its own color (MLB dominant color used for MLB players)

des_10.brief: 15-row dot plot / lollipop chart. Each row = one player. Horizontal bar or dot positioned by their gap value (peak-to-median rank). Colored by league — MLB players stand out because 10 of the 15 rows are MLB. Annotation pointing to Andres Torres (838, the biggest gap): 'biggest spike in the data'.
des_10.rationale: A lollipop lets the name labels be fully readable while still conveying magnitude. Color encoding by league makes the MLB dominance obvious at a glance.

des_11.label: Browse all 78 — filterable table

content.initial_state: 78-row table showing league, name, peak_year, peak_rank, median_rank, worst_rank, seasons. Sorted by league then peak_rank. Row backgrounds tinted by league color.
content.trigger: Dropdown filter (by league) above the table; column headers are clickable for sorting. Asterisk on any player whose peak was 2016 or 2017 with a tooltip: 'Career may still be active after 2017 data cutoff — see Ashleigh Barty'.
content.payoff: Reader can find their team, their sport, their era. Full data transparency.

des_11.brief: 78-row HTML table with sticky header, league color strips on the left edge of each row, filter chips above for leagues, sortable columns. Post-2015 rows have a small asterisk. Includes a 'Caveat: The dataset ends in 2017' footnote with the Ashleigh Barty example.
des_11.rationale: Table + filter delivers data transparency and lets the reader find their personal entry point (their favorite team/sport/era).

des_12.label: Closing — after the game

content.prompt: Quiet empty stadium after the game, single forgotten ball at the tunnel, warm tungsten lights, melancholy, teal-amber, no people, no text

des_12.brief: Full-bleed image under the closing paragraphs. Tone: after the game, everyone gone, one forgotten ball at the tunnel. Matches the teaser's palette for visual bookending.
des_12.rationale: Bookends the piece with mood. The teaser shows the lit moment; the closer shows the dark afterward.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial with warm amber accents
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first — hero image, then prose with charts interspersed, bookended by images
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Serif title and pull quotes (Playfair Display or similar); sans-serif body (Inter or similar). Large stat callouts at ~120px. Dark background (#0b1220), warm amber highlight color (#f0a43a), cool blue secondary (#4a9bc4), muted grey for non-highlighted data (#3a4455). Section dividers thin horizontal rule in muted grey.
